pr_body:
fix https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/6749

The idea is that we want arrows to be able to cross frames. Investigating that, it seems better if bound arrows (either start/end binding is set) to not be part of frames at all.

I'm sure I've skipped some cases.

New rules:

> An arrow can be a child of a frame only if it has no binding (either start or end) to any other element, regardless of whether the bound element is inside the frame or not.
>
> This ensures that when an arrow is bound to an element outside the frame, it's rendered and behaves correctly.
> 
> Therefore, when an arrow (that's a child of a frame) gets bound to an element, it's automatically removed from the frame.
> 
> Bound-arrow is duplicated alongside a frame only if the arrow start is bound to an element within that frame.

issue_context.title: Arrows cannot cross between frames
issue_context.body:
Frames are a great addition! I'm currently using them showing ownership of separate parts of a system. These separate parts need lines between them to show how the systems communicate. When I draw a line between boxes in two separate frames, the line is attached to one frame, and cannot be seen in the other frame. It would be great if you could see elements over the top of frames.

![image](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/assets/16151065/652dfadb-66ff-42df-a4f1-7205af401a81)
comments:
It is possible to make the arrow cross the frames. You just need to use the hand tool and move the center of the arrow between the 2 frames to make it overlap. 

While moving the arrow using the hand tool, make sure the hand does not cross over any of the frames, or else the arrow will go inside the frame as seen in the above image.

We were discussing this with @ryan-di during implem. It was not quite clear how it should render.

There are two options:

![image](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/assets/5153846/11fa8337-03eb-4af6-a9c7-59ba49ffbcc6)


EDIT: ok, lookin at it, option A makes more sense 😅

Another question is about when exporting the frame as image. Possibly don't render the arrow when exporting either frame 1 or 2.
